title: Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Patients With Major Depressive Disorder, Third Edition
authors: Gelenberg AJ, Freeman MP, Markowitz JC, Rosenbaum JF, Thase ME, Trivedi MH, et al.
journal: American Psychiatric Association; approved May 2010, published October 2010
funder: not stated in the guideline; developed under the direction of the APA Steering Committee on Practice Guidelines.
authorConflicts: For May 2005 to May 2010, all six Work Group members disclosed consulting, speakers bureau, advisory board or research support relationships with pharmaceutical companies, including antidepressant manufacturers such as Eli Lilly, Pfizer, GlaxoSmithKline, Wyeth, Forest and Lundbeck; the consultant reported none. An Independent Review Panel without current industry relationships found no evidence of bias.
result: An antidepressant medication is recommended as an initial treatment choice for mild to moderate major depressive disorder [I] and definitely should be provided for severe disorder unless ECT is planned [I]; for most patients an SSRI, SNRI, mirtazapine or bupropion is optimal [I]; depression-focused psychotherapy alone is also recommended as an initial choice for mild to moderate disorder [I]. SSRIs generally should be tapered over several weeks; discontinuation-emergent symptoms are more likely with paroxetine than sertraline and typically resolve without treatment over 1 to 2 weeks, although some patients have more protracted syndromes.
